Top candidates: Common_Smut (black spore masses), Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mold), Gibberella_Disease (pink/red mold).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
The Gibberella reference is very similar - yellow kernels at base, rotted top with fungal growth. Let me use my 4th view on another Gibberella reference to confirm.

This confirms the pattern. The second Gibberella reference (left ears) shows exactly what the test image has: yellow healthy kernels at the base, dark rotted mass at the tip/top with white-gray fungal growth. Gibberella ear rot characteristically starts at the silk end and progresses downward.

The test image matches Gibberella_Disease closely:
- Ear husk removed/rotted away
- Yellow kernels in lower portion (still healthy)
- Dark rotted mass concentrated at the top (silk end) with white/gray mold
- Typical tip-down progression of Gibberella infection
